about.title: Saratoga Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Saratoga residents rely on nearby Santa Clara County medical facilities for everything from routine checkups to major surgery, and most visits go as expected. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages medication, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there's a shorter notice window, a required expert review, and specific rules under MICRA that shape how a case moves forward. We evaluate medical negligence claims and explain, in plain terms, whether a case may be worth pursuing. Our goal is simply to help you get informed guidance quickly, without cost or obligation, so you're not trying to sort through medical and legal complexity alone while also recovering physically.

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Timeline
items.desc: California medical malpractice claims generally must be filed within one year of discovering the harm, and no later than three years from the injury itself, with a required 90-day pre-suit notice. We help review your case quickly so these deadlines aren't missed.

items.title: Cases Require Qualified Medical Review
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California requires a qualified medical expert to support most claims. Our team works with the right resources to determine whether the standard of care was actually breached.

items.title: No-Cost, No-Obligation Consultation
items.desc: We offer free initial consultations, and we typically handle these claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Saratoga?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discover the harm, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself, whichever comes first. A 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider is also typically required before filing. Because these deadlines can be affected by specific facts, it helps to have us review your timeline early.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law requires showing that a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care, and that this failure caused harm. A poor result on its own, even after a difficult surgery or complicated diagnosis, isn't enough. A qualified medical expert typically has to review the case to determine whether negligence actually occurred.

items.question: Does your firm handle malpractice cases from Saratoga hospitals or clinics?
items.answer: Yes, we evaluate medical malpractice claims tied to local Saratoga-area providers. We handle these cases directly and assess whether your situation qualifies for further review. There's no cost or obligation for an initial consultation.
